dedupe_keys.name: global distribution of cattle horses goats sheep and buffaloes at 1 km 2000 to 2022

description: These Land & Carbon Lab maps give annual 1 km densities and headcounts of cattle, sheep, goats, horses and buffaloes worldwide from 2000 to 2022. An areal-regression spatiotemporal machine learning framework (random forest with spatial blocking and feature selection) links subnational census counts from 55,336 administrative units in 147 countries to 128 environmental and socio-economic predictors, allocates animals over an annual layer of land potentially used for livestock, and adjusts totals to FAOSTAT national figures. Outputs include densities with 95 per cent prediction intervals and FAOSTAT-consistent headcounts, as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs on Zenodo, free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; the method is described in a PeerJ article, and WRI lists annual updates. Caveats: the provider stresses that pixels are a statistical redistribution of coarse census counts, not observed herds or farms, and accuracy varies with census detail. For simulation it gives animal exposure for drought, heat stress, flood and disease outbreak scenarios, and livestock water and feed demand in agricultural supply models. Related catalogue records include the global grassland class and extent maps and FAOSTAT.
name: Global distribution of cattle, horses, goats, sheep and buffaloes at 1 km, 2000 to 2022
provider: Land & Carbon Lab, via the WRI Data Explorer
